interface.name: mx_shell_surface_manager_v1

description.summary: assign shell roles to layer surfaces

interface.description:
This interface lets a shell tell the compositor what each of its zwlr_layer_surface_v1 surfaces is for. Layer shell alone orders surfaces only by layer; a role places a surface among the shell's other surfaces and the apps, and for some roles changes how input reaches it. Everything else about the surface (anchors, size, exclusive zone, keyboard interactivity) stays as layer shell defines it.
A role takes effect only while the surface is on the top or overlay layer. On the bottom or background layer it has no effect, and the surface stacks as layer shell defines.
While in effect, surfaces stack front to back by role, in this order:
1. prompt 2. edge 3. bar 4. osd 5. osk 6. view 7. overlay-layer surfaces without a role 8. a fullscreen toplevel and its dialogs 9. top-layer surfaces without a role 10. other toplevels, then the bottom and background layers
The one exception is osk: while a prompt surface has keyboard focus, osk stacks above prompts instead, so the prompt can be typed into. Several surfaces with one role stack among themselves newest first.
The compositor may offer this interface to privileged clients only. It may also give a layer surface without a role one by its own means, such as treating the namespace "osk" as the osk role.

entry.name: already_set
entry.summary: layer_surface already has a role or was already configured

enum.name: role
enum.description: What a layer surface is for. Each role's description says where it stacks and how input reaches it; see the interface description for the whole order.

entry.name: view
entry.description: A screen of the shell that covers the apps, such as a home screen, an app switcher or a settings panel. It stacks above every toplevel, a fullscreen one included, and below every other role. Input reaches it as layer shell defines.

entry.name: osk
entry.description: An on-screen keyboard. It stacks above views and below OSDs, except while a prompt surface has keyboard focus: then it stacks above prompts, so the prompt can be typed into.

entry.name: osd
entry.description: Short-lived feedback such as a volume or brightness indicator. It stacks above the keyboard and views, below bars.

entry.name: bar
entry.description: Persistent shell chrome such as a status bar, usually with an exclusive zone. It stacks above OSDs, below edge regions.

entry.name: edge
entry.description:
An input-only region along one edge of the output, for swipes in from that edge. The edge is the one the surface's anchors span: the surface is anchored to it, and to both edges beside it or to neither. Swipes away from that edge, towards the middle, are inward.
Edge regions stack above bars, below prompts. The compositor need not draw them, so their content may never be shown: it still sends frame callbacks, and answers wp_presentation feedback as discarded.
Pointer input passes through to what is beneath. A touch that begins on the region is held until the compositor decides whose it is. An inward swipe gives the whole touch sequence, from its start, to the region. Any other movement, the touch ending, another touch point, or the touch staying still for a short time gives it to what is beneath. Distances and times are compositor policy.

entry.name: prompt
entry.description: A question from the system that the user must answer, such as a power menu or a password dialog. It stacks above every other role, except the keyboard while a prompt has keyboard focus.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager object. Roles assigned through this interface remain valid.

request.name: set_role

description.summary: assign a role to a layer surface

request.description:
Assign a shell role to a zwlr_layer_surface_v1. The surface keeps it for as long as it exists.
This request must be made before the initial wl_surface.commit that precedes the first zwlr_layer_surface_v1.configure event. Calling it after the surface has been configured or calling it more than once on the same zwlr_layer_surface_v1 raises the already_set protocol error. A role value this version doesn't define raises invalid_role.
